hed: Alfecca Meridiana: The Southern Star of Corona Australis
dek: A detailed look at a prominent star in the constellation Corona Australis, revealing its significance and characteristics.
body:
Alfecca Meridiana, also known by its Bayer designation Alpha Coronae Australis, stands out as a notable star within the constellation Corona Australis. Positioned at approximately 19.16 hours of right ascension and about -37.90 degrees declination, this star is a key feature in the southern sky, forming part of the rich tapestry of stellar figures that have guided observers for centuries.

Although precise distances and luminosities are often subject to measurement challenges, Alfecca Meridiana is generally regarded as a bright, physical object candidate, contributing to the constellation's distinctive celestial shape. Its role as a figure star within recognized star asterisms and its inclusion in various star catalogues underscore its importance in celestial navigation and cultural astronomy.

The star’s exact physical properties, such as its magnitude and spectral type, are drawn from widely acknowledged star catalogues, making it a reliable reference point for astronomers and stargazers. Its position near other prominent stars enhances its role as an anchoring feature in star maps and observational guides.

In the context of scientific observation, Alfecca Meridiana exemplifies the stable, enduring nature of fixed stars that serve as crucial markers in the night sky. Its consistent position allows for reliable navigation and aligns with historical and modern practices of celestial mapping.

As part of the complex structure of the Southern Hemisphere’s stellar landscape, Alfecca Meridiana continues to inspire amateur and professional astronomers alike. Its presence in the constellation Corona Australis offers a beautiful example of the intricate artistry of the universe’s celestial arrangements, reminding us of the enduring human fascination with the stars.
